findings.title: MegaETH skips every later candidate of a block once one transaction fills the block budget for new state, and the specification leaves the order of reconsideration to the sequencer
findings.difference: MegaETH caps new state at 1,000 entries per block and per transaction. Once a block reaches a block-level runtime limit, every later candidate is skipped for that block. Ethereum has no per-block cap on new state.
findings.mechanism: Unchanged on 2026-11-26. One transaction that creates 1,000 new storage slots brings the block to BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT. BlockLimiter::pre_execution_check (limit.rs line 765 on mega-evm main) then skips every later candidate of that block before execution, a modifyLiquidity, take or burn sent to the PoolManager among them. A skipped transaction gets no receipt and, in the words of the specification, may be reconsidered in a later block. When it runs later it meets the same checks in the PoolManager: unlock, the onlyWhenUnlocked gate and the delta count at the end of unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), and it pays or receives what the pool state of that later block gives, within the caller's own limits. The PoolManager holds no time-dependent state that a delay of one block could change. The specification gives no rule for the order of reconsideration, so whether N filling transactions close N blocks to a chosen exit or only to the candidates behind each one is the sequencer's choice, and the sequencer is a privileged party.
findings.impact: No funds move and no balance is lost. Swaps, liquidity removals and claim burns of other users can be delayed by about one second per filling transaction. A longer delay depends on the sequencer's unpublished queue rule.
findings.preconditions: The base fee stays near its floor. The sequencer does not filter the sender. The attacker pays for 1,000 new state entries per block it fills.
findings.mitigations: Exits under load can be forced through an L1 deposit. The operator can raise the block state growth limit above the per-transaction limit, price state growth more steeply, or put skipped candidates ahead of later arrivals.

For this unit only. Monad: 'latest' maps to a Proposed block and 'safe' to Voted (docs.monad.xyz block states page); a proposed block can be dropped only by leader or vote failure, which no ordinary account controls, so a reorg needs the validator set (operator). MegaETH: a single sequencer orders and seals mini-blocks (docs.megaeth.com/architecture), so any reorg needs the sequencer (operator). Bridges that act on 'latest' rather than 'finalized' are an integration hazard outside the PoolManager.
The specification fetched on 2026-11-26 still says the transaction gas limit must fit a 'sequencer-configured per-transaction gas cap' and gives no value. The bound in earlier cycles stands.
